name: The Divine Warring and the Settling
summary: The first quarrel. In creation's morning, Solvane claimed the sun as his alone; Luneth refused, holding the moon a shared secret. Their pride wounded the song itself — the first tear in the Veil, made not by malice but by vanity. The Settling ended it: day and night would rotate, neither would rule the other's realm, and the Veil was woven as a peace treaty with seven neutral grounds marked upon the world.

participants.name: Solvane
participants.note: demanded first voice in the song

participants.name: the Chorus
participants.note: the lesser gods forced both to arbitrate rather than unmake creation

course_of_events.what: Solvane names the day and claims sole authorship of light; Luneth answers by drawing the shadow long across his morning.
Their duelling verses fall out of harmony; the song tears — the first wound in the Veil. Stars gutter. Something on the far side notices.
Orbren strikes an anvil-note that neither can talk over; Mornath holds the hourglass sideways until both agree to speak in turn.
Day and night rotate by covenant. The Veil is woven as a peace-treaty membrane. Seven True Places are crowned as neutral ground where all voices may be heard and none may dominate.

key_places.name: The First Wound
key_places.description: The original tear in the Veil, sealed by the Settling but never healed — sages say every later wound, including the Quiet, echoes its shape.

key_places.name: The Seven True Places
key_places.description: Seven sites where the song runs strongest, crowned neutral by covenant. All are lost to memory and map; at least one lies under the Stone Crown, another under a flooded ruin.

consequences: No single god may dominate — the covenant every later divine dispute has broken or invoked.
The Veil exists as treaty, not wall: thinning it is breach, not accident.
The Seven True Places become the world's most consequential lost treasure map.
remembrance: No mortal witnessed it; everything known comes from the gods' own oaths and the Deep Tongue creation-sagas. Dwarven smiths still strike an anvil-note to open disputes — 'speaking like Orbren' means forcing arbitration.
adventure_hooks: A True Place is found. Whoever claims it holds a piece of the original covenant — every church on Aurelith will want a word.
The First Wound's 'shape' appears in a new scar near the Quiet. Either history repeats, or something is copying it.
An Old Weaver text claims the Settling had a third signatory whose name was struck from the song.
